The real 50-row bound is checked by counting identical seeded rows and preserving tagged row order. Stored and published rows are distinct. Timestamp classes include numeric strings, fractions and integers beyond the JavaScript safe range.
Host private files and controlled platform ports. Android cross-process log writes, actual OS exits, AtomicFile behavior and renderer diagnostics presentation remain separate.

Host JVM fixtures exercise renewal-specific methods. WorkManager scheduling, platform intent delivery, encrypted-storage internals, resident and external effects remain outside the campaign.

abstractions: Two Activity/bridge identities, fixed renderer generation, exact or foreign binding, one bound account snapshot and selected elapsed-time boundaries.

Closed bridge port mirrors installed Capacitor bridge assignment and virtual intent reentry. Exact sanitized object forwarding during load preserves the authenticated cold receipt. A copied argument or public delivery takes the ordinary path.
Power entry uses exact product pin and readback members with controlled credential and Android permission ports. Tile has at most one pending controlled unlock callback.
No Activity launches, microphone capture, Android Settings or app runtime process. OS authority and delivery are external.

stateMapping.kind/phase/attempt/claim/completeBinding: Exact selected journal operation class, durable status, immutable admission and retained result
stateMapping.proof/status/notice/visible: Synthetic child evidence, persisted notification receipt and active-list outcome
stateMapping.live/process/method/requestedBinding/rep: Bridge retirement/reconstruction, chosen readback and projected result class
stateMapping.noticeReads/deletionReads/reminderReads/: Closed receipt accesses and separately observed durable write attempts

abstractions: One selected row, absent/foreign request addresses, exact known operation and bounded receipt equality classes.
The selected binding fences unresolved reminder receipt lookup. Passive selected-reminder reads retain a marker and summary, with the full result preserved for exact get.
Native worker and journal run on the host JVM. Deletion provider, notification manager and ReminderEnvelope are closed synthetic inputs, with pre- and post-commit store failure.

The kinds note-write, calendar-write, files-write, camera-capture, browser-navigate and view-only are journaled operation classes with no native receipt reader: NoNativeProofNeverSettles and ViewOnlyNeverRecoversToSuccess state that no notice, reminder or deletion recovery call settles them. These kinds are model-only; the host-JVM replay does not drive them, and the shared coordinator's own saved-receipt reconciliation for camera, Calendar and Notes results is not modeled here.
Coordinates, rounded hit tests, shadows and event dispatch stay native-library/Pixel evidence.
Pause represents Android cancellation; exact activity lifecycle sequencing requires signed-device qualification.
Session, profile and sensitive-overlay authority remain BrowserSession/BrowserSiteState.

stateMapping.credential/remoteOwner/grants/reset: Synthetic raw credential classes, remotely reported owner/grants and pending reset
stateMapping.generation/grant/owner/boundCredential/c: Selected encrypted row, exact owner, decimal history progress and durable history-route refusal count
stateMapping.latestGeneration/attempt/admitted/config: Actual generation assignment and admitted epoch with one held account response
stateMapping.periodic/catchup/schedules/cancels: Closed WorkManager command names, generations and request counts
stateMapping.workGeneration/workEpoch/workReply/histo: Exact worker snapshot and result, page reads and reconstruction
stateMapping.notice/tap/visible/posts/allowed/observa: Ledger and exact pending/consume/release, synthetic posting and foreground readback

abstractions: Three grants, two remote owners, three credential equality classes, one retained notice and one held transport callback across two bridge instances.

Four-page Worker checkpoint, 20-digit decimal cursor examples, synthetic work commands, selected HTTP outcomes and pre/postcommit storage failures. History-only403/409 completes after three durable refusals; an accepted page resets the counter.401 and verified account/grant revocation remain immediate. Further deliveries of an already completed failing job are outside this bounded schedule.

Targeted retirement fences only matching saved or pending grants. Consume checks the exact still-current tap after remote admission. Releasing a question remains local cancellation. Executor refusal releases only its own unadmitted attempt, advances the settled epoch and preserves the durable selection.
Android and provider effects are closed. WorkManager delivery, real durable storage and installed notification/Activity enforcement remain outside the campaign.

stateMapping.rows/now/writes/restarts: Selected durable consent, exact scope/revision, revocation and expiry across host reconstruction
stateMapping.owner/generation/foreground/transport/ca: Controlled admission, review foreground and source identity
stateMapping.readOwner/readSource/readGeneration/read: One retained read across controlled source suspension
stateMapping.reply/replyAt/requestKind/grantReply/eve: Actual returned metadata and bounded projected result with source port counts

abstractions: Two owners and two exact grant slots, opaque revision equality, one selected owner day, and one held source operation.

Synthetic storage, resident, Calendar and Reminder ports only. No device/provider action or model egress.

stateMapping.epoch/retired/ticket/ticketEpoch/expires: Actual volatile lifecycle, one canonical stored tuple with clock/deadline, and captured worker handoff plus observed originating epoch
stateMapping.reviewPhase/reviewEpoch/reviewResult/com: One reviewing CAS, queued UI delivery epoch, visible dialog, terminal resolution and rejected overlapping request
stateMapping.provider/granted/locked/focused/dialogFo: Controlled provider revision and platform admission inputs
stateMapping.stageRefused/stageCount/staged: Synthetic enqueue outcome, exact target comparison and side-effect-attempt count

abstractions: One selected scoped occurrence, four exact tuple coordinates with opaque hash equality, two provider drift classes, one held final permission result and one review dialog.

The initial inspection and worker provider reread are macrosteps except the explicitly held permission result. Multi-ticket capacity, real CalendarProvider mutation and downstream journal settlement are outside this component.
The ticket insertion and pause clear share a generation monitor. This models ticket authority at insertion, not delivery of an already-committed reply after a later pause.

stateMapping.epoch/lease/leaseEpoch/dialog/prepareRes: Actual bridge epoch, current lease, observed dialog and bridge results
stateMapping.durable/writes/compareAttempts/pauseRefu: Closed store bytes, accepted CAS sequence, attempt counts and injected contention
stateMapping.held/heldExpected/claimedEpoch/enabledEp: Final enable read suspension, captured CAS snapshot class, lease generation and committed enable provenance
stateMapping.cloudWriteAllowed/deletionAllowed: Actual exact saved-consent and deletion-refusal outputs

abstractions: One bridge, one exact owner/destination, pre-marked local source with no events and one held consent worker. Synthetic platform and credential store, no provider writes.
Saved bytes are partitioned into absent, unchanged disabled, and enabled classes for this schedule. Enabled operation provenance is observed via accepted store writes.

One bridge monitor orders enabled CAS against local lease retirement. A successful durable pause fences the old enable, and an exhausted pause CAS reports unavailable without fabricating durable revocation.
One current editor and account; eligibility and same-editor/account checks are input facts. Exact Android InputConnection behavior and physical Cartesia output remain device gates.

Six bounded generation advances; every emitted Quint transition is compared with the actual Java gate in test/keyboard-dictation.test.mjs. The recording-id fence and sensitive field admission have separate host Java scenarios.
Network transport, Android media capture and framework voice IME selection are not established by this gate model.

Closed credential, PCM, provider and HTTPS ports exercise one transport call per trace. Direct guard and PCM decoding have declared synthetic boundaries. Installed authority and provider acceptance remain separate.
One review lease, with exact queued/admitted/retired state and successful return counts. The JVM adapter executes all 81 ordered four-call histories.
Android Activity/AlertDialog and worker scheduling, effect staging and actual device acceptance are separate obligations.

stateMapping.stage[voice]: The voice-adapter stopping chain and mediaUnconfirmed
stateMapping.waiting/refused/refusal: A successor awaiting the previous retirement, and the coded refusal it receives
stateMapping.stopConfirmed: A confirmed native stopPlayback made by confirmSpeechRetirement
stateMapping.recorderOpen/entryLatched/entryMessage: startTranscription: the open recorder and the message an entry is refused with

abstractions: Four independent chains, each idle, playing, retiring, recovering or closed; at most six requests and one restart.
A request made while speech plays on its chain retires that speech and waits; who cancels the predecessor is not distinguished.

The voice surface and read aloud stay closed until the app process restarts. App speech and Cloud app speech ask native to stop playback once per request on a closed chain: a confirmed stop admits the request, a refused one keeps the chain closed with the restart message.
Native cancel and stop are one confirmed-or-unconfirmed settle step (see RendererSpeechChunk). Starting a voice conversation on a closed voice chain is refused the same way as Transcribe.

stateMapping.phase: speakChunk from listener registration to the settled dispose
stateMapping.preparePending/playback/nativePlayback: The preparation promise, the adopted playbackId and a playback native produced
stateMapping.finishedSignal/pendingOutcome/result: The finished promise, the reason the chunk ended and what speakChunk resolves or rejects with
stateMapping.strict/queue/retries: strictDrain, queue and the busy-speaker retries

abstractions: One chunk; three listeners. The source retries a busy speaker without a count limit until aborted; here the speaker is busy at most twice per chunk.
Listener registration is one step per listener. The 100 ms retry wait and the 500 ms bounded cleanup are nondeterministic ticks.
A terminal event seen while playing or waiting for the speaker retires the chunk in the same task: no abort or retry timer comes between the event and its retirement.
Synthesis text, playback identity checks and the execution requirement are folded into the prepare result classes ok, busy and error.
The 20-minute passage limit and multi-chunk passages of speakLocalText are outside this model.

stateMapping.active/started/responded/terminal: The variables of the same names in streamNativeAgent
stateMapping.outcome/failure: The completed promise and whether a failure carries beforeDispatch
stateMapping.chunks: Body chunks enqueued after the response

abstractions: One stream; response status classes 200, 401, 429 and other; at most three chunks.
Frame validation, the 2 MB limit and content-type checks are one valid/invalid class. The turn limit, the idle limit and the caller signal are one abort action.
Assumption: native rejects requestStream only before it sent anything to the runtime.
Parsing of the event stream body (readLocalAgentStream) is outside this model.

stateMapping.epoch/owner/recovering/closed: recoveryEpoch, the restore owner epoch, recoveringLegacy and the destroyed plugin
stateMapping.stage: accepted, snapshot taken, and the Cloud identity read outside every lock
stateMapping.legacy/legacyAtRequest: the retained legacy production credential and its state when the restore was accepted
stateMapping.slot/commitsSinceRequest: the Cloud credential slot writer and shared sign-in commits since the request
stateMapping.answer/refusals: the plugin call result and login-active refusals

abstractions: Six epochs and one saved credential. The legacy journal, exact-byte recheck and encrypted storage are AlphaCredentialStore primitives covered by existing tests.

The shared sign-in client is a controlled port: only its entry points, cancel, matching return and commit reservation are represented. The client reserves the credential intent when a Google attempt is accepted or a code is sent and stores the key later under that guard; the model joins the two into signInCommits.
An already expired saved credential is not offered and answers that nothing was restored; the expired refusal is only the expiry passing between the snapshot and the token check.

The replay in specs/quint/refinement/native/saved-sign-in-recovery.mjs runs the real AlphaCloudSignInPlugin with the credential store and the shared client as ports, so legacy, slot and stage are port state there. Scenario and simulation evidence otherwise; no Keystore, installed-upgrade or Cloud claim.

stateMapping.admitting/generation/session/requestingP: NativeMapsLocation admitting, generation, session and requestingPermission
stateMapping.admission: the single start() in flight: its ticket, its session, whether it is one-shot and the await it is parked on, including the cleanup of the session it replaced or of its own failed watch
stateMapping.listeners/watches/cleanup/failedCleanups: ElizaLocation listener handles, native watch ids and the removals stop() awaits
stateMapping.lastStart/deliveries/errors: how start() settled for its caller, and the onFix and onError calls made per session
stateMapping.selfStopped/cleanupErrors: stops made by report() and by a one-shot fix, and the onError call such a stop makes when its cleanup is unconfirmed

abstractions: Three sessions and eight generations. One owner object; the Maps screen holds three (route origin, guidance, agent), each an instance of this model.
Fix validation is one boolean: a stale, future or malformed fix is reported as an error and stops the session.
The browser permission-request cancel and heading or speed fields are not modeled. The native plugin's own permission and provider state is external.
The native event carries no watch identity, so every registered listener hears every fix; only the session in place delivers it.

A session that registered no listener has nothing to clean up: its stop settles at once and a start that replaces it puts the new session in place in the same step. A stop between start() and that step is not modeled.
Both listener registrations of one start are one step.
A start rejected because the cleanup it waited on was unconfirmed has one outcome, whether that cleanup belonged to the replaced session or to its own failed watch.
A stop is drawn one time in four so sampled traces reach a delivered fix.

stateMapping.session/generation/settles/cause: One recorder Session, its settled latch and the error it settled with
stateMapping.bytes/chunks/full/truncated: Admitted bytes, kept chunks, size-limit stop and whether nonempty media was dropped
stateMapping.prefix: Bounded retained-media read before reporting a truncated recording as saved
stateMapping.adapter/finalizing/leaving/previewStoppe: The camera view recording flags and the order of finalisation and preview stop on leave
stateMapping.rows/resolved/savedGeneration/failures: Saved video rows, resolved recordings and finalisation failures

abstractions: Sizes are units with a limit of two; three recordings. The duration limit and an ended camera track are one stop event.

A chunk that would pass the size limit is left out. A retained prefix with nonempty dropped data needs a successful media read before saving. The prefix read port groups an unreadable prefix and its deadline into one refusal. Microphone loss and frame-draw failures are the recorder error.
No reachable state has a recorder session cancelled by the stopped preview: leaving finalises first, so the cancelled branch of stopPreview is unreachable.

Trace replay: test/quint-video-recorder.test.mjs replays simulator traces step by step against BrowserVideoCapture with MediaRecorder, the camera track and timers as ports; the Camera view half (shutter, leaving, preview) is supplied by the driver as the calls the camera adapter makes and compares the observed state after every step. It is bounded evidence for the sampled traces, not a refinement proof or device acceptance.

stateMapping.loaded/busy/closed/hidden/playing: Editor flags and the hidden-page disposal
stateMapping.edit/submitted: The live edit and the copy handed to save
stateMapping.saves/outcome/aborted: Save calls, the settled result and the abort signal

abstractions: Trim positions are tenths of a second over a four-tenths source. Rotation and centre crop are opaque values.
The trim clock is a pure function checked over boundary values.

Trace replay: test/quint-video-edit-review.test.mjs replays simulator traces step by step against openVideoEditReview mounted in a DOM with the media element and the save callback as ports and compares the observed state after every step. It is bounded evidence for the sampled traces, not a refinement proof or device acceptance.

stateMapping.status/parameters/replace/attempt: The stored edit receipt status, encoded parameters with mode and owning attempt. An absent receipt after prepared-editor cancellation is the explicit abandoned terminal; later saves are refused.
stateMapping.inflight: Save attempts suspended between claim and commit
stateMapping.sessionActive/recordedRevision/sourceRev: The actual editor session and original photo row against the per-row mutationRevision recorded in its receipt. External metadata edits and trash each advance that original revision; adding a distinct copy row does not.
stateMapping.copies/replaces/reportedNoCopy: Committed copy rows, committed in-place replacements, and a recovery read that reported no write

abstractions: One receipt, three save attempts, two non-identity parameter sets and two modes. Rendering is an opaque suspended step.

Session expiry is an explicit clock boundary. Closing an unclaimed prepared editor deletes its receipt (abandoned); recovery reads retain cancelled receipts. Acknowledged receipt forgetting and age-based pruning are outside the single-operation replay.

The CopyReceipt adapter executes real Chromium canvas and IndexedDB save, recovery, cancellation and rollback schedules, comparing all state fields from actual receipts, sessions and persisted rows. Two source mutations test retirement and mode fences; physical durability, native editing and device acceptance remain separate.

stateMapping.liveTask/pages: MainActivity.liveInstance and the instances that loaded a bridge and page; a handed-off instance never loads one
stateMapping.liveTaskId/liveTaskHome: taskKinds entry of the live task and startedAsHome, read from the first start intent of a task and kept across relaunch
stateMapping.unacked/unreliable/frontInFlight: unackedFrontStarts (cleared when the page owner resumes or receives a marked start, including the one that created it), handOffUnreliable and marked bring-to-front starts (EXTRA_FRONT_START) not yet delivered
stateMapping.starts/delivered/handOffs: external starts, the intents delivered to a page owner (own onCreate/onNewIntent or live.onNewIntent) and handOff calls

abstractions: One home task and one standard task; four external starts. Android resolves a home-type intent to the home task and every other start to the standard task.
A hand-off from an instance that shares the live task, the assistant surface and non-launcher builds are outside this model.
Moving a standard task by id and the marked front start are single outcomes; the activity-type rule is AOSP behaviour measured on an emulator, not a public contract.

The replay in specs/quint/refinement/native/home-instance-handoff.mjs plays Android's task resolution and delivery order against the real MainActivity; which task a real start reaches is not established by it.

stateMapping.epoch/accepting/stopping: lifecycleEpoch, accepting and stopping under lifecycleLock; getStatus releases stopping once the service is seen stopped with no unacknowledged credential stop
stateMapping.mutationEpoch/retryEpoch/shutdown: credentialMutationEpoch, credentialShutdownRetryEpoch and credentialShutdownRequest with the service acknowledgement of that exact request
stateMapping.startRequest/startRequestEpoch/startOwns: startRequestId, startRequestEpoch and startOwnsLaunch (true only when the start found the service stopped)
stateMapping.cancelledStarts/attachedStarts: request ids cancelled before their start arrived, and starts that attached to an admitted running resident
stateMapping.native/launchedBy/launches/commits: ElizaAgentService process state, the request whose start launched it, and committed credential mutations

abstractions: Two start requests, six lifecycle generations and three launches. Attach admission (root token, provider generation, owner) is one boolean.

A start request while a stop is latched or a credential stop is unacknowledged is the strict recheck (shutdownRetryRequired): it reissues the stop under a new request and is modeled as reissuing in the same step it is admitted, although the plugin does that on its worker.
Enrollment, pending bridge calls and the 128-entry cancellation bound are not modeled. The 15 s acknowledgement wait ends in one step; an uncertain commit is treated as an unconfirmed shutdown.

The replay in specs/quint/refinement/native/resident-start-cancel.mjs covers lifecycleStep, the machine without a credential mutation, on the whole plugin over service and Android ports; beginMutation and finishMutation are exercised only by the NativeCredentialMutation adapters.

stateMapping.home/losses/deaths/stale: MainActivity.showsHome of the launcher surface; RendererRecoveryBudget lossesInWindow and deaths; started with more than WINDOW_MS since windowStart
stateMapping.surfaces.alive/owed/owedCrash: whether the surface's WebView has a renderer, and a death of the shared renderer process (RenderProcessGoneDetail.didCrash) not yet delivered to its onRenderProcessGone
stateMapping.surfaces.createdAt/started/reportVisible: rendererDeathsAtCreate; the activity lifecycle being at least STARTED now and when onRenderProcessGone ran
stateMapping.surfaces.recovering/pendingRebuild/escap: recoveringRenderer, pendingRebuild, the native escape view, the recreation posted on the decor view (0 ms or BACKOFF_MS) and a requested recreate()
stateMapping.rendererDeaths/reclaimSpent: ghosts: renderer process deaths, and a hidden reclaim that changed the counted deaths

abstractions: One launcher surface and one assistant surface share one renderer process and budget; six renderer deaths. Up to three earlier counted crashes of the launcher's page stand for a partly spent budget.
The 60 s window is one flag: it has passed or it has not. A recreation is requested and completed as separate steps; a finishing activity and a missing System WebView are outside this model.

Reports of one death reach the surfaces in any order and any time apart. A report delayed past another surface's rebuild can leave that rebuilt WebView with a stale creation count, so its next death spends nothing (OvertakenSurfaceWitness); no device evidence says how far apart Android delivers them.

The replay in specs/quint/refinement/native/renderer-background-rebuild.mjs drives two real MainActivity instances over Android and Capacitor ports. WebView process death, activity recreation and what the user sees remain platform and device obligations.

stateMapping.phase: where the request worker submitted by request() is: waiting for one of the two workers, between its first requireOwned and the one before raw(), blocked in raw() on the transport, or returned
stateMapping.call: the request PluginCall: member of pending (open), resolved by resolveCurrent, rejected by cancelRequest (withdrawn) or rejected by invalidateOwnCalls / rejectSuperseded (superseded)
stateMapping.renderer: the caller of LocalAgentProtocol.request: waiting on the bridge promise, its signal aborted (requestNativeAgent has queued cancelRequest), cancelRequest delivered, or settled
stateMapping.withdrawable: the withdrawable map from cancelId to the request call under lifecycleLock
stateMapping.sent/withdrawnAt/answers: ghosts: requests that reached raw(), the worker phase at which cancelRequest withdrew the call, and how many times the bridge call was resolved or rejected

abstractions: Three requests and two workers; other bridge methods that share the same two workers are not modeled.
Enrollment is one step with no failure; owner mismatch, 401 handling and transport errors are folded into the transport answering.
A lifecycle change is one step that answers every pending call; the epoch that also stops their workers is represented by the call no longer being pending.

A request already on the transport is not recalled: ElizaAgentService.requestLocalAgent offers no cancellation handle, so the worker is held until the answer or the timeout and the server effect may complete.
One contact with four revisions and one agent proposal at a time; search, paging and field contents are not modelled.
Provider write success, external edits and permission changes are nondeterministic inputs.
A dispatched contact batch with a lost reply stays unknown whether it committed or not. Actual writes are environment facts in the bounded trace; no carrier or device execution is established.
One thread, up to three inbound messages and two draft texts. The reviewed radio dispatch is NativeSmsDispatch; here a confirmed review yields sent, failed or unknown.
ready collapses image admission, SMS role, permission, unlock and foreground.
One call and one agent proposal at a time; conference, call waiting and audio routes beyond speaker are not modelled.
Contact lookup returns zero, one or two matches; Telecom acceptance and remote behaviour are nondeterministic inputs.

An ambiguous placement reply consumes the approval and remains unknown whether Telecom accepted or not; the executor must propagate that rejection to the coordinator journal. Actual call state is a controlled environment fact here.
One voicemail with three generations; list paging is not modelled.
Carrier state, audio fetch, recognizer availability and transcription results are nondeterministic inputs. A cloud upload is counted, not transported.
Up to three unread threads, missed calls and new voicemails; row content and ordering are presentation.
Source loading and items cleared elsewhere are nondeterministic inputs.
